title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering to prevent regional thrashing and failed failovers
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: We observed regional thrashing and intermittent failed failovers under sustained overload when the SLO enforcer triggered backoff and circuit-breaker workflows. Root cause: a race between backoff ordering and the regional failover coordinator that allowed multiple regions to concurrently transition into load-shedding state, causing oscillation and preventing a stable failover. This hotfix stabilizes ordering by making backoff transitions idempotent and introducing an ordered, atomic transition path for SLO->CB->failover that the coordinator can observe consistently. Changes: 1) make backoff timer updates atomic with a compare-and-swap keyed by request windows; 2) add an enforcement queue that serializes state transitions per-customer per-region; 3) introduce a short, configurable grace window (default 250ms) to avoid flip-flop when metrics spike briefly; 4) add additional metrics and tracing hooks so the coordinator can assert monotonic state changes; 5) add unit and integration tests that recreate the race and validate stability; 6) add a temporary operator toggle to force stricter thresholds while we complete canary and mitigations. Testing and rollout: ran local unit/integration tests, e2e canaries in us-west1/us-east1 and eu-west1 passed under synthetic overload, load tests show elimination of oscillation on 10m sustained 2x baseline request rate. CI: initial unit failure due to missing test stub (fixed in second commit), full CI now passes. Merge: squash and merge to main; deployed as a rolling hotfix to Dedicated pools then Hosted gradually over 1 hour with observability checks. Rollback plan: feature toggle to revert grace window and ordering change; operator runbook updated. Impact: no API breaking changes, customer traffic might see briefly stricter SLO enforcement during rollout for affected tenants to stabilize failovers. Follow-ups: coordinate with on-call to monitor new metrics and bump grace window if we see false positives, and consider increasing default grace window if similar spikes continue.
